guitar.guitaristsText: Mick Ronson / Carlos Alomar / Earl Slick
guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul (Ronson) / Fender Stratocaster / Telecaster
guitar.notes: Bowie used many different guitarists across eras with no single signature instrument tied to Bowie himself; medium is appropriate given Ronson's well-known Les Paul.

tone.target: sustaining lead with tape delay and amp breakup
tone.profile: sustaining lead with tape delay and amp breakup
tone.summary: A clean, sustained signal chain utilizing a pre-amp boost for initial grit, followed by an AC30 TB/UK Vintage 4x12 combination to achieve bright, singing sustain and controlled Marshall-style breakup, finished with Tape delay and Room reverb.
corrections: favor amp breakup over pedal overdrive

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and sustain tails.
Provide initial edge-of-breakup grit and sustain boost.

alternatives.reason: Could provide more defined dirt, but Boost is better for subtle breakup.

blocks.purpose: Used as a secondary grit source if needed, but kept off to favor amp breakup.
Simulate the bright, classic British breakup and singing sustain of a Marshall-style amp.

alternatives.reason: Also suitable, but AC30 TB is better for the required bright upper mids.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British tone and bright upper mids required for the lead sound.
Enhance the upper mids and sustain while slightly tightening the low end.
No wah needed for this sustained lead tone.
Implement the required 'tape delay echo' effect.

alternatives.reason: The Tape module is ideal for true tape delay, but Digital Delay offers better control over the specific 'echo' feel required.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle studio ambience and sustain to the lead lines.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR to better capture vintage studio realism and upper-mid clarity.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic British tone and bright upper mids for lead sustain.
